title: Friction is the force that slows a sliding object
summary: Friction is an outside force that acts against sliding and makes a sliding object slow down.
body: OpenStax Physics uses a sliding box to show why motion dies away. A net outside force acts on the box and slows it. Without that force the box would keep a constant velocity. The page names the slowing force friction, and says kinetic friction is the surface force, parallel to the surface, that opposes a sliding object. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. How large that force is depends on the surfaces, which the page treats through a coefficient.
